question: A square has a perimeter of 100 cm. What is the area of the square?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the square = Perimeter ÷ 4

⇒ Side = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm

Area of square = (Side)²

⇒ Area = 25 × 25 = 625 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 625 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the square = 100 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a square = 4 × a (where a is the side length)

Area of a square = a²

 
 Side (a) = 25 cm
 Area = 625 sq cm
 Perimeter = 100 cm
 
•

 a = 25 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × a = 100

⇒ a = 100 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 25 cm

⇒ Area = 25 × 25

⇒ Area = 625 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 625 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Square

The length of the diagonal (d) of a square is given by d = a√2, where a is the side length of the square.

Area using Diagonal

The area can also be calculated directly from the diagonal length using the formula: Area = d² ÷ 2.

Incircle and Circumcircle

The radius of a circle inscribed within a square is a ÷ 2, and the radius of the circumscribed circle passing through its vertices is a ÷ √2.
